question.text: An Indian AIF manager sets up a feeder fund in GIFT City (IFSC) to pool foreign investors into the domestic master. The feeder fund is registered as a Fund Management Entity (FME) under which regulations?

explanation.text: The Logic: A GIFT-IFSC feeder fund is registered as a Fund Management Entity (FME) under the IFSCA (Fund Management) Regulations, 2025 — IFSCA is the unified regulator in GIFT IFSC and has superseded SEBI for funds based there. The Trap: Option A applies to the onshore Indian AIF (master), not the IFSC feeder. Option C (FPI) is the route foreign investors would use to invest into Indian securities directly, not the feeder itself. Option D is FEMA currency-movement regime, not fund-registration. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers IFSCA for Cat I/II/III; XIX-E tests Cat III-specific IFSC feeder structuring. Manager's Pro-Tip: GIFT-IFSC feeder structure is increasingly popular — Section 80LA of the Income-tax Act gives a 100% tax holiday on IFSC income for any 10 consecutive years in a 15-year block. Evaluate if your foreign raise justifies the setup cost.
